title: Execution from refreshed local variables
statement: Let $xs$ be a list of variable indices, $l$ a list of integers, and $loc$ and $\mu$ integer-valued functions on the natural numbers. Suppose $loc(y)$ equals the value of the list frame $l$ at index $y$ for every $y$ not in $xs$. If a statement $s$ has an execution from the state whose locals are obtained by refreshing the entries of $l$ at the indices in $xs$ with their values from $loc$, and whose memory is $\mu$, within cost $T$ and with postcondition $Q$, then it has such an execution from the state with locals $loc$ and memory $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $y\notin xs$, $loc(y)$ equals the value of the frame of $l$ at $y$
The statement has an execution from refreshed locals and memory $\mu$ of cost at most $T$ satisfying $Q$
